service_name: Solid Waste Management — Department Structure, Byelaw Fines & Grievance Enforcement
sub_service: Door-to-door/community-bin collection, cleanliness byelaw fines, Clean-up Marshal enforcement
problem_type: Littering, unsegregated waste, uncleaned premises ('Clean Aangan'), biomedical/C&D waste violations
municipality: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM / BMC)
department: Solid Waste Management Department, MCGM (Chief Engineer SWM; 24 Administrative Wards)
authority: Chief Engineer, Solid Waste Management, MCGM; ward-level Clean-up Marshals
description: This is MCGM's Solid Waste Management Department RTI Manual (Section 4(1)(b) disclosure, revised to 31.03.2015) — an organizational/administrative document, not a citizen-facing service charter. It describes: waste generation of roughly 450 gms/person/day citywide; collection split 78% door-to-door and 22% via community bins across the 24 Administrative Wards; 4 refuse transfer stations (Mahalaxmi, Kurla, Versova, Gorai) feeding the Deonar, Mulund, and Kanjur dumping grounds (the latter two under biomining projects). Enforcement runs under the 'Greater Mumbai Cleanliness & Sanitation Byelaws, 2006', which set a detailed fine schedule: littering Rs. 200; failing to maintain a clean 'Aangan' (frontage) Rs. 1,000-10,000; handing over unsegregated waste Rs. 100-500; improper biomedical-waste disposal Rs. 20,000. These byelaws have been enforced by dedicated 'Clean-up Marshals' since 15.11.2007.
procedure: Waste is collected via scheduled door-to-door pickup (78% of the city) or community bins (22%) by ward. Byelaw violations (littering, unsegregated handover, uncleaned frontage, improper biomedical-waste disposal) are enforced on the spot by Clean-up Marshals under the 2006 byelaws' fine schedule.
sla: SLA NOT FOUND — this document is an organizational/administrative manual (not a citizen-facing charter) and does not state a numeric complaint-to-resolution timeline.
escalation_procedure: On-the-spot fines under the Greater Mumbai Cleanliness & Sanitation Byelaws, 2006, levied by Clean-up Marshals: littering Rs. 200; not maintaining a clean Aangan/frontage Rs. 1,000-10,000; unsegregated waste handover Rs. 100-500; improper biomedical-waste disposal Rs. 20,000.
escalation_authority: Chief Engineer, Solid Waste Management, MCGM

faq.question: What is the fine for littering in Mumbai?
faq.answer: Rs. 200, enforced on the spot by a Clean-up Marshal under the Greater Mumbai Cleanliness & Sanitation Byelaws, 2006.

faq.question: What is the fine for handing over unsegregated waste?
Does this document state a complaint-resolution SLA?
faq.answer: No — it is an organizational RTI manual describing department structure and the byelaw fine schedule, not a citizen service-response-time charter.

citizen_guidance: Segregate waste before handover and keep your frontage ('Aangan') clean — Clean-up Marshals can fine violations on the spot (littering Rs. 200, unsegregated waste Rs. 100-500, uncleaned frontage Rs. 1,000-10,000, improper biomedical-waste disposal Rs. 20,000).
